members.evidence_quote: Decreases in measles vaccination coverage worldwide have increased the risk for larger measles outbreaks, especially in undervaccinated communities ([About Measles | CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/measles/about/index.html#cdc_disease_basics_population-who-is-at-risk)). On August 18, 2025, the [Texas measles outbreak was declared over](https://www.dshs.texas.gov/news-alerts/texas-announces-end-west-texas-measles-outbreak), having comprised 762 confirmed cases, 99 hospitalizations, and a second measles-associated death. Although the source of this outbreak remains unknown, internationally imported cases have been associated with outbreaks among other close-knit U.S. communities with low vaccination coverage (*3*,*4*). High population coverage with 2 MMR vaccine doses is the most effective public health intervention for preventing measles ([Measles Vaccination | CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/measles/vaccines/index.html?CDC_AA_refVal=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.cdc.gov%2Fvaccines%2Fvpd%2Fmmr%2Fpublic%2Findex.html)).
